xmax stores transaction ID of deleting or updating transaction

query: What attack does OAuth 2.0 PKCE protect against according to RFC 7636, and how does code challenge verification work?

ground_truth.attack: Authorization code interception attack on public clients
key_facts: Protects native and single-page apps unable to hold a client secret
Client generates code_verifier and derives code_challenge (SHA-256 / S256)
Authorization server validates SHA-256(code_verifier) == code_challenge upon token exchange

query: What is the purpose and behavior of DNS TTL and negative caching according to RFC 2308?

ground_truth.concept: DNS caching lifetime and NXDOMAIN/NODATA negative caching
key_facts: TTL defines duration a resolver may cache a positive DNS record
RFC 2308 specifies negative caching for non-existent domains (NXDOMAIN)
Negative cache duration taken from SOA record MINIMUM field

query: What is the difference between TCP and UDP in packet headers, state transitions, and connection lifecycle?

ground_truth.concept: Transmission Control Protocol vs User Datagram Protocol
key_facts: TCP has 20-60 byte header; UDP has fixed 8-byte header
TCP uses 3-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK) and 4-way FIN teardown
TCP maintains connection states (LISTEN, SYN_SENT, ESTABLISHED, etc.)
UDP is stateless and connectionless with no delivery guarantee

query: What are the technical trade-offs between B-tree, BRIN, GIN, and GiST indexes in PostgreSQL for time-series and full-text data?

key_facts: B-tree is general-purpose, high cardinality, log(N) lookup
BRIN is lightweight for physically sorted time-series data with small index footprint
GIN is inverted index optimal for composite items, full-text search, and JSONB contains (@>)
GiST is balanced tree suitable for geometric, range, and nearest-neighbor search

query: How does Apache Kafka guarantee partition message ordering during consumer group rebalance and producer idempotence?

key_facts: Ordering is guaranteed strictly within a single partition, not across topics
Producer idempotence uses producer_id (PID) and sequence numbers to deduplicate retries
Consumer group rebalances reassign partitions using group coordinator and cooperative sticky protocols

query: Compare Redis Sentinel vs Redis Cluster for high availability, split-brain mitigation, and quorum failover mechanics.

key_facts: Sentinel provides master-replica monitoring and automatic failover for single logical keyspace
Cluster provides horizontal sharding across 16,384 hash slots with decentralized gossip-based failover
Sentinel requires quorum of sentinels; Cluster requires majority of master nodes
Split-brain mitigated via min-replicas-to-write and min-replicas-max-lag

query: Explain the difference between Kubernetes Startup, Liveness, and Readiness probes and how container restart policies interact with them.

key_facts: Startup probe disables liveness/readiness until container finishes initialization
Liveness probe determines if container needs to be killed and restarted
Readiness probe determines if Pod receives network traffic via Service Endpoints
Restart policy (Always, OnFailure, Never) controls kubelet action on liveness failure

query: Explain how Conflict-free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs) resolve concurrent edits: State-based (CvRDT) vs Operation-based (CmRDT).

ground_truth.authoritative_source: Shapiro et al., Comprehensive Study of CRDTs
key_facts: CvRDT (State-based) sends entire state; merged via bounded semilattice least upper bound (LUB)
CmRDT (Operation-based) sends commutative mutation operations requiring exactly-once causal delivery
Strong Eventual Consistency guarantees convergence without central coordination

query: Compare PostgreSQL and MongoDB for a high-write IoT telemetry workload considering consistency, indexing, horizontal scaling, and operational complexity.

ground_truth.concept: Relational vs Document Store for IoT Telemetry
key_facts: PostgreSQL offers strict ACID, BRIN indexing, timescaledb partitioning, but horizontal write sharding requires Citus
MongoDB offers native sharding, flexible BSON schemas, time-series collections, but higher storage footprint and eventual consistency tradeoffs

query: Compare Rust vs Go for high-throughput network microservices considering memory footprint, concurrency model, and developer velocity.

key_facts: Go has M:N green-thread scheduler (goroutines), GC pauses, fast compilation, high developer velocity
Rust has zero-cost abstractions, no GC, compile-time borrow checker, Tokio async runtime, minimal memory footprint

query: Compare GraphQL vs REST APIs for mobile client bandwidth optimization, over-fetching prevention, caching strategies, and schema evolution.

key_facts: GraphQL eliminates over/under-fetching with client-specified queries, but complicates HTTP network-level caching and query complexity attacks
REST leverages native HTTP status codes and CDN caching, but requires multiple round-trips or tailored endpoints

query: Compare Redis vs Memcached for distributed application caching, eviction policies, memory efficiency, and multi-threading.

key_facts: Memcached is multi-threaded, simple key-string store with slab allocation and LRU eviction
Redis is single-threaded event loop with rich data structures, persistence (RDB/AOF), replication, and flexible eviction (LRU, LFU, TTL)

query: Compare AWS Lambda vs Cloudflare Workers for edge computing considering cold starts, V8 isolates vs microVMs, runtime constraints, and pricing models.

key_facts: Cloudflare Workers uses V8 isolates with zero/sub-5ms cold starts, shared OS process, restricted Web APIs
AWS Lambda uses Firecracker microVMs with container isolation, 100-500ms cold starts, full Node/Python/Custom runtimes, and VPC access
